title: Future forms review
note: Choice unit: will / going to / present continuous / present simple / future continuous / future perfect / time clauses / future in the past · 8 meanings x 6 items · 48 items · built to live 2026-08-06 (cloud run 4) · 2026-08-19: negatives contracted (do not -> don't) — textbook register for a B1/B2 speaker; full forms still accepted

cards.title: Future forms — choose, don't re-teach
cards.title_cz: Budoucí tvary — volba, ne znovu učení
cards.body: At B2 you already know the forms. This unit is about **which form fits the meaning**: plan, prediction, arrangement, timetable, process in the future, completed before a future point, and **future seen from the past**.
cards.body_cz: Na B2 tvary znáte. Jde o to, **který tvar sedí k významu**: plán, předpověď, domluva, jízdní řád, proces v budoucnosti, hotové před budoucím bodem a **budoucnost z pohledu minulosti**.

cards.title: The seven futures
cards.body: Each form answers a different question about the speaker's viewpoint, not about the time itself.
cards.body_cz: Každý tvar odpovídá na jinou otázku o pohledu mluvčího, ne o samotném čase.

table.caption: Meaning → form
rows: It will probably be cold tomorrow.
I am going to look for a new job.
I am meeting the client at three.
In progress at a future point
They will be waiting for us at the station.
By Friday she will have finished the report.
would · was going to · was about to
He said he would be late.

cards.title: will vs be going to
cards.body: The decision point is what separates them: **will** = you decide as you speak; **be going to** = you decided before, or the evidence is in front of you right now.
cards.body_cz: Rozhoduje moment rozhodnutí: **will** = rozhodujete se právě teď; **be going to** = rozhodli jste se dřív, nebo je důkaz přímo před vámi.
points: That bag looks heavy — I will take it. (decided now)
I am going to look for a new job. (decided before)
It is very dark — it is going to rain. (evidence now)

cards.title: No will in a time clause
cards.body: After **when, before, after, as soon as, until** and after **if**, English uses a present tense even though the meaning is future. The other half of the sentence carries the will.
cards.body_cz: Po **when, before, after, as soon as, until** a po **if** používá angličtina přítomný čas, i když jde o budoucnost. Will nese druhá polovina věty.
points: I will call you when I arrive. (not: when I will arrive)
As soon as the rain stops, we will leave.
If it is warm tomorrow, we will walk to the park.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Most B2 errors are the right form in the wrong slot, not a broken form.
cards.body_cz: Většina chyb na B2 je správný tvar na špatném místě, ne rozbitý tvar.
points: will after when / as soon as / if
will for an arrangement already fixed with someone (use present continuous)
be going to for a timetable (use present simple)
will where the past viewpoint needs would / was going to
